new_value: FALSE ALARM on deeper analysis — no route-poison, severity overstated. Traced the full route-installation path: EVERY route install goes through SignatureVerifiedDao::verify_signature (router.rs:720 -> verify.rs:55-102), which enforces origin == ygg_addr_from_pubkey(pinned_key) (verify.rs:79) and schnorr-binds origin+origin_sequence+unsigned_bytes (targets) via dao_origin_digest. A forged DAO with a routable 02xx/GUA origin for a target the attacker does NOT key-own fails signature at the root (BadSignature/IidMismatch) -> no route is installed -> NO route-poison. The relay gate I flagged (node.rs:612-672) is an anti-relay OPTIMIZATION, not the route-installation security boundary; the 7331 comment (node.rs:630-638) already documents that for routable sources the origin proof is the mandatory downstream signature check. The gate being loose for routable sources wastes at most LoRa airtime forwarding a DAO the root will reject — a bounded resource concern, not a correctness/security hole. Pre-migration the gate was equally loose for routable sources (same_interface matched link-local only). Closing as not-a-bug; re-filing the actual residual as P2 defense-in-depth (routable-source DAOs skip the cheap early anti-relay check and cost airtime to forward junk the root discards).
